clips.title: The lethal trifecta: the AI agent security risk you need to know
clips.why: The three-part risk the threat model walks for every part of the platform, in under two minutes.
look: The three ingredients: private data, untrusted input, and a way to send things out.
Why removing one ingredient is enough to break the attack.
clips.after: Our threat model removes private data from the sandbox (fake seed data only) and narrows the way out to a short allow-list.

clips.title: Security Chaos Engineering - Winning at Security “Whack-a-Mole” • Aaron Rinehart • GOTO 2021
clips.why: Security chaos engineering: instead of hoping a security control works, cause the situation it should handle and watch what happens.
look: The definition: experiments that test security controls on purpose.
The use cases, and how close they are to our probes and egress drills.
clips.after: Our design review's probes and the blocked-site drill are small security experiments: each must be refused and must leave a trace.

clips.title: The DiRT on Chaos Engineering at Google • Jason Cahoon • GOTO 2021
clips.why: Why Google breaks its own systems on purpose every year, and what kinds of things it tests.
look: The reasons to test disasters before they happen.
The list of what they test: systems, but also people and processes.
Compare with our four drill areas: VM, agent, outside services, people.
clips.after: Our drill kit is a very small version of the same idea, run before the pilot and again after every big change.

clips.title: Back to Basics: Chaos Engineering with AWS Fault Injection Simulator
clips.why: The AWS service our VM drills use: experiment templates, targets and safety checks.
look: How an experiment template names an action and its targets.
The stop conditions that end an experiment early.
How a running experiment is watched.
clips.after: The VM drills run FIS templates such as terminate-instance and send-spot-instance-interruptions against drill tickets' VMs in the ai-agents account.

practice.q: Put the four parts of a drill in order.
items: Start a run on a drill ticket
Wait for the state the playbook promises, with a deadline
Assert on what people would see: status, thread, Jira, metrics, VMs
practice.why: The same shape for every drill makes the kit easy to read and to extend.

practice.q: Which tool causes the fault in a VM drill, such as "a VM killed mid-run"?

options.text: AWS FIS experiments, such as terminate-instance
options.why: FIS breaks the real machine the way AWS would, with stop conditions for safety.

options.text: A fixture ticket that asks Nova to edit a CI workflow
options.why: That is an agent drill: it tests a wall against the agent's own actions.

options.text: A drill-only switch that makes the gateway answer 529

practice.q: Finish the deadline of the Stop drill so it fails if Stop waits for the first reminder (2 seconds on a drill ticket).
practice.hint: Anything shorter than the reminder; the lab uses one second.
practice.why: A deadline shorter than the reminder proves that Stop ended the wait at once, not at the next timer.

practice.q: Why does every probe in the design review have two pass conditions?

options.text: The attempt must fail, and it must leave a trace in the logs or an alert
options.why: A wall that holds silently lets an attacker keep trying unseen until one attempt works.

options.text: It must fail twice in a row to rule out luck
options.why: Repeating does not help if nobody can see the attempts.

options.text: It must fail from two different VMs
options.why: One sandbox is enough for a probe. The second condition is the trace.

practice.q: The threat model says the sandbox holds no private data. Which leg of the lethal trifecta does that remove?

options.why: Fake seed data only, no patient data, no staging or production credentials: an injected prompt finds nothing worth stealing.
Tickets, code, Slack and web pages are untrusted, and Nova must read them to do its job.

options.text: A way to send things out
options.why: That leg is narrowed by the proxy and the broker, not removed: Nova still pushes, comments and posts.
